task.description: Write test/specs/REQ-151.md and test/letflow/engine/lua/sandbox_test.exs covering every acceptance criterion in REQ-151, testing against the real implementation (lib/letflow/engine/lua/sandbox.ex) directly rather than only restating the design doc's prose.
acceptance_criteria: a single sandbox-construction function exists and a repo search for the library's own state-construction call across lib/ shows that function as the only call site, with the real output quoted

a test evaluates each of io.open, io.write, os.execute, os.exit, os.getenv, os.remove, os.rename, os.tmpname, load, loadfile, dofile, require, package, debug, and string.dump from INSIDE a script obtained from that function, and asserts each is nil or raises
if any custom :sandboxed list is passed, a test asserts the DEFAULT denials still hold after it (at minimum os.execute and load); if no custom list is passed, the moduledoc says so and names REQ-152
the moduledoc states LUA-03 restatement with all three reasons
the moduledoc states LUA-04 restatement (structural, no rejection path)
the deny-set is written out explicitly with a per-entry reason, and coroutine's availability is an explicit recorded decision
mix test and mix compile --warnings-as-errors both pass with real output quoted

result.summary:
Wrote test/specs/REQ-151.md (7 test-case groups, each with a rationale distinct from a restatement of the acceptance criterion, plus an AC-to-test-case traceability table) and test/letflow/engine/lua/sandbox_test.exs (30 ExUnit tests, all constructing Lua.t() exclusively via Letflow.Engine.Lua.Sandbox.new/0 or new/1, never Lua.new/1 directly).

Before writing assertions, empirically probed the real implementation via `MIX_ENV=test mix run` against a scratch script (not trusted from the design doc's prose alone): found that every one of the 28 deny-set paths, once passed to Lua.new/1's `sandboxed:` option, becomes a real raising function when CALLED, regardless of the design doc's 'installed vs. not installed / vacuous' classification -- `Lua.sandbox/2` always writes a raising callable at the given path. Referencing a denied path (e.g. `return os.execute`) returns a truthy NativeFunc; only calling it (e.g. `return os.execute('ls')`) raises `Lua.RuntimeException` with a '<name> is sandboxed' message. `string.dump` and `coroutine` are the true exceptions -- both evaluate to plain `nil` since no deny-set entry exists for either path. This empirical finding is recorded explicitly in both the spec and the test module's moduledoc, and shaped every per-path test to call (not just reference) the denied function, matching AC2's literal 'nil or raises' wording against actual runtime behavior rather than the design doc's installed/vacuous framing.

Test coverage: (1) AC1 -- `System.cmd("grep", ["-rn", "Lua.new(", "lib", "--include=*.ex"])` run from inside the test asserts exactly one hit, inside sandbox.ex. (2) AC2 -- one test per named path (io.open, io.write, os.execute, os.exit, os.getenv, os.remove, os.rename, os.tmpname, load, loadfile, dofile, require, package, debug all assert_raise Lua.RuntimeException on call; string.dump asserts nil). (3) AC3 -- two tests: default denials (os.execute, load) hold via Sandbox.new/0, and again via Sandbox.new/1 with an arbitrary/future-looking options keyword list, proving the one options surface this module exposes today does not narrow the deny-set. (4) debug's specific metatable/upvalue functions (getmetatable, setmetatable, getupvalue, setupvalue) individually asserted to raise -- the concrete instance of the design's 'central finding.' (5) coroutine asserted nil, not sandboxed. (6) smoke test: math.floor, string.format, table.insert all succeed normally. (7) six moduledoc-content assertions via Code.fetch_docs/1 (not raw file read) covering AC4 (LUA-03's three reasons: loadstring/5.1, jit/ffi/bit vacuity, SBX-1 property-not-mechanism), AC5 (LUA-04 structural/bytecode), and AC6 (coroutine decision text, REQ-152 named for the custom-list disposition).
